paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average answer change percentage across sequential follow-up turns, with separate lines for cases where the initial answer was correct versus incorrect. The x-axis is labeled “Turn Number,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer turns from 1 to 7 with ticks at each integer. The y-axis is labeled “Average Change Percentage (%),” uses a linear scale, and is shown from 0 to 50 with regularly spaced tick labels every 10 percentage points. One line corresponds to “Initial Correct Answer,” drawn in red with circular markers connected by a solid line; it starts at about 4% at turn 1, rises to about 6% at turns 2–3, increases to about 12% at turn 4, and then remains at about 12% through turns 5–7. The other line corresponds to “Initial Incorrect Answer,” drawn in orange with circular markers connected by a solid line; it begins at about 16–17% at turn 1, increases to about 25% at turns 2–3, jumps to about 49% at turn 4, and then stays at about 49% from turns 5 through 7.
